title: Correlation, parlays and prop combos
description: The brief asks us to determine correlation values. We can honestly deliver the estimator, the treatment rules and the empty cells — not the numbers, because a correlation coefficient in this project must be measured from a joint sample we hold, and the sample (historical prices and settled joint outcomes) is exactly what is blocked at GAP-01. Publishing invented rho values would be the single most damaging fabrication available here: every parlay decision downstream would inherit it. So the rho column is blank by design and flagged.

sections.title: A. What we are measuring
sections.description: Not 'are these events related' — they obviously are — but 'how much does treating them as independent overstate the combined price'.

rows.definition: Pearson correlation of the two leg win indicators, on the population of games both legs were offered on, at the moment of pricing (pre-game).
rows.note: This is the quantity a parlay price actually depends on, not the correlation of underlying stat lines. Computed as corr(I_A, I_B) over our settled sample; reported with a bootstrap interval and an n.

rows.definition: fair_parlay_prob / (p_A x p_B) - 1, i.e. how wrong multiplying single-leg probabilities is.
rows.note: For positively correlated legs this is positive: the true combined probability is higher than the product, so a bettor multiplying singles believes they have more value than they do. For negatively correlated legs it inverts. This ratio, not rho, is what a parlay decision should read.

rows.definition: Simulate the game (score process, drive outcomes, player stat generation), evaluate both legs inside one simulation, and read the joint probability directly.
rows.note: Preferred to analytic correlation because props are non-linear functions of the same simulated game (a QB's yards and his receiver's catches share drives, possessions and game script, not a linear factor). The simulator is engine/correlation.py; its inputs are our own distributions, and it inherits S2's unverified parameters honestly.
Derived, and cross-checked against the note in the fetched academic source; used as the hurdle in G-2.

rows.definition: Product of the individual legs' break-evens, corrected by the measured dependence.
rows.note: The reason parlays are dangerous even when each leg has an edge: if the operator's combined price already reflects the dependence, our apparent 'extra value from correlation' is not extra.

rows.definition: A non-SGP parlay may never contain two offers whose outcomes might be related; if they slip through, the operator may void the affected legs; an SGP with a void or pushed leg is repriced from the odds available at bet placement.
rows.note: Verified from operator house rules as filed with a state regulator, and mirrored on a licensed property's own rules document. Version-stamped, so re-check before coding settlement.

rows.definition: Nevada requires books to maintain win-to-write percentages for each sport and for sports parlay cards as a separate line.
rows.note: The regulatory framework itself treats parlays as a structurally different product. What the actual percentage is, we have not verified, so no number is published (GAP-08).

sections.title: B. Pair table — rho deliberately blank, sign prior labelled as a prior

rows.mechanism: Both driven by the same scoring process; a high-scoring script raises the favourite's win probability and the Over's simultaneously.
rows.treatment: SGP only; never allow as a plain parlay leg pair — the house rules bar related outcomes outside an SGP.
rows.measure: corr of settled indicators over every season we have prices for; bootstrap 2000 resamples

rows.mechanism: Nearly the same event: a first-half lead is a large share of a game win, especially for a heavy favourite.
rows.treatment: Treat as one exposure for bankroll purposes regardless of how it prices; this is the clearest 'two bets, one position' case in the book.
rows.measure: corr plus the conditional P(win game | win half) on our own results

rows.mechanism: Shared pace and shared scoring environment, offset by the zero-sum element of a closer game; sign is genuinely ambiguous a priori.
rows.treatment: Priced only from the joint simulation, never from multiplication.
rows.measure: the pair that best tests whether our simulation reproduces the operator's SGP price

rows.mechanism: Arithmetic containment: Team A's points are part of the total.
rows.treatment: Allowed in SGP; flagged as high-dependence in the exposure cluster so it cannot silently double a view.

rows.mechanism: Same drives, same targets, and game-script dependence: a trailing QB throws more to his top option.
rows.treatment: The canonical prop-combo pair: priced only jointly; singles remain independent bets.
rows.measure: joint simulation from our own possession model, validated against settled data once we have it

rows.mechanism: Shared play-action view of the game script rather than a mechanical link.
rows.prior_sign: positive if the view is 'run the ball, keep it low'
rows.treatment: Allowed; must be shown as one view with one budget, since the two legs are the same bet in different clothes.
rows.measure: conditional distribution of team points given attempt volume in our logs

rows.mechanism: Common cause: pressure reduces dropbacks and completions; but sacks can also come on obvious-passing long downs, which cuts the other way.
rows.treatment: Refuse in parlays until measured; this pair is where a 'sack + under' narrative becomes a coin flip dressed as a thesis.
rows.measure: measure both the marginal and the script-conditioned correlation before allowing it

rows.leg_b: Prop on that player's availability-driven usage (e.g. backup RB attempts)
rows.mechanism: Our deficiency index creates the dependency: if the starter is Out, the usage leg becomes both more likely and better priced by us than by the market.
rows.prior_sign: positive by construction of the feature
rows.treatment: This is the one place where correlation is generated by our own information edge rather than by market mechanics — so it must be disclosed as model-derived, not measured from prices.
rows.measure: compare the pair's joint probability under our availability scenarios versus the base case

rows.mechanism: Weak but non-zero: shared weather systems, shared officiating philosophy slate, shared rest patterns and identical market hours.
rows.prior_sign: near zero, but not exactly zero
rows.treatment: Cross-game parlays priced as independent, with a residual dependence allowance; do not market the independence as a feature.
rows.measure: test on the slate-level residual correlation of our CLV, not on outcomes

rows.leg_a: Same-team, opposite-direction legs (e.g. team total O and opponent spread U)
rows.mechanism: Negatively dependent through margin; also a common accidental hedge that looks like two edges.
rows.treatment: Flag and net the exposures: a negative-correlation pair can be an unintended partial refund of a bad bet rather than a second bet.
rows.measure: corr on settled indicators; publish the net exposure view

rows.leg_a: Player prop leg that is an injury-status proxy
rows.mechanism: The league asks operators not to offer wagers whose subject is a player injury, and treats a single person's one-play decision as prohibited.
rows.treatment: Hard refuse at the compliance gate before correlation is even considered.

rows.mechanism: Score-first is a script marker: it correlates with the eventual winner and weakly with the total.
rows.treatment: Allowed in SGP only; check whether the operator's SGP price already captures it before claiming value.
rows.measure: event-level resimulation from our drive model

rows.leg_a: Any two legs from the same game in a plain (non-SGP) parlay
rows.mechanism: Prohibited by house rule, so the question is academic outside an SGP.
rows.treatment: Reject at bet construction. If the offer somehow exists, we assume it will be voided on settlement, and we score it that way in any backtest.

rows.leg_a: Prop-combo with a voidable leg (player ruled out after bet placement)
rows.mechanism: Settlement mechanic, not statistical dependence — but it dominates realised parlay value because the operator reprices rather than pays.
rows.treatment: Model the void-and-reprice path explicitly in backtests; a combo built on a Friday designation is a bet on the reprice rule as much as on the player.
rows.measure: read the current filed rule version and encode the exact repricing convention

rows.leg_a: Parlay of 4+ positively correlated SGP legs
rows.mechanism: Error amplification: an rho estimate that is wrong by 0.05 compounds across legs, so the combined 'edge' can be pure model error.
rows.treatment: Cap SGP legs at 3 in v1 and require the joint price to be quoted, not derived from our singles.
rows.measure: sensitivity of combined fair value to +/-0.05 perturbations of each pairwise rho, published per bet

sections.title: C. Reading the blank rho column
sections.description: Why the most valuable thing this table does is refuse to fill itself in.

rows.explanation: We were asked to determine correlation values. The determination is that the values require a joint sample of prices and settled outcomes we do not yet hold, and that the estimate cannot be sourced from any official NFL or regulator page — the league does not publish betting lines at all. A number written here today would be decoration.

rows.item: What we can compute without any purchase
rows.explanation: Correlations between two markets whose outcomes are determined by official game results (spreads, totals, team totals, stat props) can be measured from historical scores alone, and score history is derivable from official game data we are permitted to collect for internal use. That is the first thing to build after the collection decision (Q-09) is made: it closes C-01, C-02, C-04, C-10 and most of the prop pairs at zero cost. It gives outcome correlation, but not correlation-at-the-priced-moment, which is what parlay value actually needs.

The pricing side: the operator's posted SGP price against its own singles at the same second. That is the only way to test whether the operator has already taken the correlation, and it is the difference between an edge and an artefact. Hence S-01.

Singles only. A parlay built on an assumed correlation is a bet whose variance we cannot bound, and a strategy whose variance we cannot bound cannot be sized, which means it fails G-1 and G-10 by construction regardless of its hit rate.
